Towards the latter part we had the welcome assistance of Charlie Churcher, rapidly returning to form, and in one match at Imber Court, both him and Harry. Charlie, however, proved the fitter of the two and finished third to Morris of S.A.C.
Morris, the Police champion, won the 880 Yards and Alf Orton ran well to credit us with third place. Rene Howell gained us first place in the 1 Mile and V.
Jack Wigley won the 100 Yards for the home club, with Dicky Dumbrill in second place, a position he also occupied in the 220. Morris won the 880 for the Police and V.
Morris, in the 880 Yards, in the fast time of 2 mins. 0.7 secs. Jack Frost also beat Morris in the 440, with Bob Wise in third place.

A few weeks later Harry further improved on this time when, again at Motspur Park, he returned the fast time of 46.10.6, half a minute in front of Jim Morris, S.A.C.
Marshall, our new Army member, Morris won from Kemp and Coleman in a new championship best of 50.3s. This was followed by the Junior which was won by Coxall in 52.8s just outside the record.
In other events, the least said about them the better, although our new lad Morris was unlucky not to reach the semi-final of the 440 yards.
Ron Holtum secured 2nd place in both 100 yards and 220 yards. This was followed by a win with Morris in the 440 yards in the time of 50.8secs.

In the 4 x 440 yards our team of Alan Sexton, Jackson, Davies and Morris were third in their heat and did not qualify for the final according to placing, but imagine their surprise when they learned that they had in fact qualified as the fastest losers, and they eventually finished 4th in the final.
Results :- Captains Team (A), Vice-Captain's Team (B) 100 yds.Senior-1, I.Mayers; 2, D.Carter; 3, B.Morris 10.0 s. 100 yds.Junior- 1, C.Ryan(B); 2, C.Cornelius(A). 10.6 s.
We seem to have gathered a fine quartet of 440 men in Dollimore, Jackson, Leroy and Morris. They won their heat in 3 min. 22.4 sec. and went on to beat the rest in the final in 3 min. 23.7 sec.

Ryan and Hennings again took first two places in the Junior 220 yds. but C.Jones had to be content with 2nd place to Gibbs of Herne Hill, Whilst Morris, who is now a recruit at the Police Training School scored 4th place for the police.

Morris, Eldridge and Leroy, you will soon have to face opposition from within. Edwin Hawkins was another to excel in the London Schools' Championships, finishing 2nd in the Long Jump, and thus gaining his London badge.
Our 'B' team of Keown, Morris, Beecham, and Stevenson walked exceedingly well and only lost 3rd team position by 2 points. Will Belderson was awarded the Sir J.Coleman Cup.
Although the ultimate winner Morris forged ahead with two laps of 60.6 each, Richard held his form well and over the last 150 yards was fast catching the leaders.
